chain.label: Extended jackscrew lubrication interval approved
chain.trigger: Alaska Airlines' extended lubrication interval and the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) approval of that extension

chain.label: Inadequate lubrication of jackscrew assembly
chain.trigger: there was no effective lubrication on the acme screw and nut interface at the time of the Alaska Airlines flight 261 accident

caused_by.evidence: increased the likelihood that a missed or inadequate lubrication would result in excessive wear of the acme nut threads

chain.label: Excessive acme nut thread wear
chain.trigger: the acme nut threads on the accident airplane's horizontal stabilizer jackscrew assembly wore at an excessive rate

caused_by.evidence: the excessive and accelerated wear of the accident jackscrew assembly acme nut threads was the result of insufficient lubrication, which was directly causal to the Alaska Airlines flight 261 accident

chain.label: Extended end play check interval approved
chain.trigger: Alaska Airlines' extended end play check interval and the FAA's approval of that extension

chain.label: No fail-safe mechanism for acme nut thread loss
chain.trigger: the absence on the McDonnell Douglas MD-80 of a fail-safe mechanism to prevent the catastrophic effects of total acme nut thread loss

chain.label: Acme nut threads sheared, jackscrew jammed
chain.trigger: the acme screw and nut jammed, preventing further movement of the horizontal stabilizer until the initial dive

caused_by.evidence: the worn threads inside the horizontal stabilizer acme nut were incrementally sheared off by the acme screw and were completely sheared off during the accident flight
allowed the excessive wear of the acme nut threads to progress to failure without the opportunity for detection
the absence of a fail-safe mechanism to prevent the catastrophic effects of total acme nut thread loss contributed to the Alaska Airlines flight 261 accident

chain.label: Initial dive: jam released by trim motor activation
chain.trigger: the accident airplane's initial dive from 31,050 feet began when the jam between the acme screw and nut was overcome as a result of the operation of the primary trim motor

caused_by.evidence: release of the jam allowed the acme screw to pull up through the acme nut, causing the horizontal stabilizer leading edge to move upward, thus causing the airplane to pitch rapidly downward

chain.label: Torque tube low-cycle fatigue fracture
chain.trigger: the low-cycle fatigue cracking severely reduced the load capability of the torque tube during the 10-minute period between the initial and second and final dive, causing it to fracture

caused_by.evidence: the screw's lower mechanical stop was restrained by the lower surface of the acme nut until just before the second and final dive about 10 minutes later

chain.label: Vertical stabilizer tip fairing brackets fail
chain.trigger: the cause of the final dive was the low-cycle fatigue fracture of the torque tube, followed by the failure of the vertical stabilizer tip fairing brackets, which allowed the horizontal stabilizer leading edge to move upward significantly beyond what is permitted by a normally operating jackscrew assembly

caused_by.evidence: cause of the final dive was the low-cycle fatigue fracture of the torque tube, followed by the failure of the vertical stabilizer tip fairing brackets

chain.label: Final dive: uncontrollable nose-down pitch
chain.trigger: the resulting upward movement of the horizontal stabilizer leading edge created an excessive upward aerodynamic tail load, which caused an uncontrollable downward pitching of the airplane from which recovery was not possible

caused_by.evidence: created an excessive upward aerodynamic tail load, which caused an uncontrollable downward pitching of the airplane from which recovery was not possible

chain.label: Water impact
chain.trigger: the airplane impacted the Pacific Ocean about 2.7 miles north of Anacapa Island, California

caused_by.evidence: the airplane impacted the Pacific Ocean near Port Hueneme, California

chain.label: Fatal injuries to all occupants
chain.trigger: The 2 pilots, 3 cabin crewmembers, and 83 passengers on board were killed, and the airplane was destroyed by impact forces

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was destroyed by impact forces
